results.title: gcd stabilisation and the reduced polynomial

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.cubic_profile_gcd_stabilisation_and_primitive_shape
declarations.docstring:
**gcd stabilisation and the primitive shape (`long243:res:gcdshape`).**

For a positive orbit `C (n+1) + D n = a n * C n`, `D (n+1) = a n * D n` whose
exceptional set against the cubic profile `A * n * (n+1) * (n+2) + B` has zero
lower density: `6 * A` is a positive integer `M`; every state gcd divides `M`;
the state gcd is eventually a positive constant `g`; and on that tail the
quotients `C n / g`, `D n / g` satisfy the primitive recurrences and both
coprimality relations, while the scaled profile is
`(m / 6) * n * (n+1) * (n+2) + c` for an integer `m > 0` and `c = ±1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cubic_profile_gcd_stabilisation_and_primitive_shape
    (a C D : ℕ → ℕ) (A B : ℚ) (hA : 0 < A)
    (hCpos : ∀ n, 0 < C n) (hDpos : ∀ n, 0 < D n)
    (hC : ∀ n, C (n + 1) + D n = a n * C n)
    (hD : ∀ n, D (n + 1) = a n * D n)
    (hzero : ZeroLowerDensity
      {n : ℕ | (C n : ℚ) ≠ A * (n : ℚ) * ((n : ℚ) + 1) * ((n : ℚ) + 2) + B}) :
    ∃ M : ℤ, 0 < M ∧ (M : ℚ) = 6 * A ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, (Nat.gcd (C n) (D n) : ℤ) ∣ M) ∧
      ∃ g N : ℕ, 0 < g ∧
        (∀ n, N ≤ n → Nat.gcd (C n) (D n) = g) ∧
        ∃ m c : ℤ, 0 < m ∧ (c = 1 ∨ c = -1) ∧
          (∀ n : ℕ,
            (A * (n : ℚ) * ((n : ℚ) + 1) * ((n : ℚ) + 2) + B) / (g : ℚ)
              = (m : ℚ) / 6 * (n : ℚ) * ((n : ℚ) + 1) * ((n : ℚ) + 2) + (c : ℚ)) ∧
          (∀ n, N ≤ n →
            C (n + 1) / g + D n / g = a n * (C n / g) ∧
            D (n + 1) / g = a n * (D n / g) ∧
            Nat.Coprime (C n / g) (D n / g) ∧
            Nat.Coprime (C n / g) (C (n + 1) / g) ∧
            0 < C n / g ∧ 0 < D n / g)

challenge.statement:
theorem cubic_profile_gcd_stabilisation_and_primitive_shape
    (a C D : ℕ → ℕ) (A B : ℚ) (hA : 0 < A)
    (hCpos : ∀ n, 0 < C n) (hDpos : ∀ n, 0 < D n)
    (hC : ∀ n, C (n + 1) + D n = a n * C n)
    (hD : ∀ n, D (n + 1) = a n * D n)
    (hzero : ZeroLowerDensity
      {n : ℕ | (C n : ℚ) ≠ A * (n : ℚ) * ((n : ℚ) + 1) * ((n : ℚ) + 2) + B}) :
    ∃ M : ℤ, 0 < M ∧ (M : ℚ) = 6 * A ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, (Nat.gcd (C n) (D n) : ℤ) ∣ M) ∧
      ∃ g N : ℕ, 0 < g ∧
        (∀ n, N ≤ n → Nat.gcd (C n) (D n) = g) ∧
        ∃ m c : ℤ, 0 < m ∧ (c = 1 ∨ c = -1) ∧
          (∀ n : ℕ,
            (A * (n : ℚ) * ((n : ℚ) + 1) * ((n : ℚ) + 2) + B) / (g : ℚ)
              = (m : ℚ) / 6 * (n : ℚ) * ((n : ℚ) + 1) * ((n : ℚ) + 2) + (c : ℚ)) ∧
          (∀ n, N ≤ n →
            C (n + 1) / g + D n / g = a n * (C n / g) ∧
            D (n + 1) / g = a n * (D n / g) ∧
            Nat.Coprime (C n / g) (D n / g) ∧
            Nat.Coprime (C n / g) (C (n + 1) / g) ∧
            0 < C n / g ∧ 0 < D n / g)

results.label: long243:res:reduciblecase
results.title: coprimality and irreducibility
results.statement_markdown: *On the primitive tail, $`\gcd(a_n,v_n)=1`$, the multipliers at distinct indices are pairwise coprime, infinitely many of them exceed $`1`$, and the cubic $`Q_{m,c}`$ of (3) is irreducible over $`\mathbb{Q}`$.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR11.primitive_zero_density_paper_multiplier_lemma
declarations.docstring:
Integer-scale form of the full paper lemma, with the exact unshifted
polynomial and the original zero-density hypothesis. All scale conversions
are performed in the body, and the unit conclusion is proved before use.
declarations.statement:
theorem primitive_zero_density_paper_multiplier_lemma
    (a u v : ℕ → ℕ) (m c : ℤ) (T : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m)
    (hv : ∀ n, T ≤ n → 0 < v n)
    (hnum : ∀ n, T ≤ n → u (n + 1) + v n = a n * u n)
    (hden : ∀ n, T ≤ n → v (n + 1) = a n * v n)
    (hcop : ∀ n, T ≤ n → Nat.Coprime (u n) (v n))
    (hzero : ZeroLowerDensity {n : ℕ | (u n : ℤ) ≠ m * risingBinomial n + c}) :
    (c = 1 ∨ c = -1) ∧
    (∀ n, T ≤ n → Nat.Coprime (a n) (v n)) ∧
    (∀ i j, T ≤ i → T ≤ j → i ≠ j → Nat.Coprime (a i) (a j)) ∧
    (∀ N, ∃ n, max T N ≤ n ∧ 1 < a n) ∧
    (∀ B N, ∃ p j : ℕ, Nat.Prime p ∧ B < p ∧ max T N ≤ j ∧ p ∣ a j) ∧

results.label: long243:res:squarespec
results.title: square specialisation
results.statement_markdown: *Let $`f\in\mathbb{Q}[T]`$ be irreducible with root $`\alpha`$, and let $`H\in\mathbb{Q}[T]`$ satisfy $`H(\alpha)\ne0`$. If for all but finitely many primes $`\ell`$ every root $`r\in\mathbb{F}_\ell`$ of the reduction of $`f`$ has $`H(r)`$ a square in $`\mathbb{F}_\ell^\times`$, then $`H(\alpha)`$ is a square in $`\mathbb{Q}(\alpha)^\times`$.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.squareSpecialisation
declarations.docstring:
**`long243:res:squarespec`**, with no hypothesis: if `f ∈ ℚ[T]` is irreducible with root
`α`, `H (α) ≠ 0`, and for all but finitely many primes `ℓ` every root `r` of `f` modulo `ℓ` has
`H (r)` a nonzero square modulo `ℓ`, then `H (α)` is a square in `ℚ(α)`.
declarations.statement: theorem squareSpecialisation : SquareSpecialisation

unfolds.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.SquareSpecialisation
unfolds.text:
def SquareSpecialisation : Prop :=
  ∀ (L₀ : Type) [Field L₀] [Algebra ℚ L₀] (α : L₀) (f H : Polynomial ℚ),
    Irreducible f → Polynomial.aeval α f = 0 → Polynomial.aeval α H ≠ 0 →
    ∀ (d : ℕ), 0 < d → ∀ G J : Polynomial ℤ,
    G.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) = Polynomial.C (d : ℚ) * f →
    J.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) = Polynomial.C ((d : ℚ) ^ 2) * H →
    (∃ N : ℕ, ∀ ℓ : ℕ, ℓ.Prime → N < ℓ → ∀ r : ZMod ℓ,
        (G.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod ℓ))).eval r = 0 →
        (J.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod ℓ))).eval r ≠ 0 ∧
          IsSquare ((J.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod ℓ))).eval r)) →
    ∃ β ∈ IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ ({α} : Set L₀),
      β ≠ 0 ∧ β ^ 2 = Polynomial.aeval α H

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.squareSpecialisation_holds
declarations.docstring:
**`long243:res:squarespec`, unconditionally.**  The statement of
`ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.SquareSpecialisation`, written out in full.
declarations.statement:
theorem squareSpecialisation_holds :
    ∀ (L₀ : Type) [Field L₀] [Algebra ℚ L₀] (α : L₀) (f H : Polynomial ℚ),
      Irreducible f → Polynomial.aeval α f = 0 → Polynomial.aeval α H ≠ 0 →
      ∀ (d : ℕ), 0 < d → ∀ G J : Polynomial ℤ,
      G.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) = Polynomial.C (d : ℚ) * f →
      J.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) = Polynomial.C ((d : ℚ) ^ 2) * H →
      (∃ N : ℕ, ∀ ℓ : ℕ, ℓ.Prime → N < ℓ → ∀ r : ZMod ℓ,
          (G.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod ℓ))).eval r = 0 →
          (J.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod ℓ))).eval r ≠ 0 ∧
            IsSquare ((J.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod ℓ))).eval r)) →
      ∃ β ∈ IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ ({α} : Set L₀),
        β ≠ 0 ∧ β ^ 2 = Polynomial.aeval α H

results.label: long243:res:transportsquare
results.title: the square forced by the numerator recurrence
results.statement_markdown: *Write $`\kappa=m/6`$ and $`\eta=6c/m`$, so that $`Q_{m,c}(n)=\kappa f(n+1)`$ for $`f(T)=T^3-T+\eta`$. Then $`\alpha^2-1`$ is a square in $`\mathbb{Q}(\alpha)^\times`$ for a root $`\alpha`$ of $`f`$.*

results.label: long243:res:scaletwelve
results.title: classification of the scales
results.statement_markdown: *Let $`m`$ be a positive integer, let $`c\in\{-1,1\}`$ and $`\eta=6c/m`$, and suppose $`T^3-T+\eta`$ is irreducible over $`\mathbb{Q}`$ with a root $`\alpha`$ such that $`\alpha^2-1`$ is a square in $`\mathbb{Q}(\alpha)^\times`$. Then $`m=12`$.*

results.label: long243:res:modseven
results.title: two incompatible four-term residue patterns
results.statement_markdown: *For $`Q_{12,1}`$, every sufficiently late four-index window beginning at $`n\equiv0\pmod7`$ contains an exceptional index. For $`Q_{12,-1}`$, the same holds for windows beginning at $`n\equiv1\pmod7`$. In either case, $`\underline d(S)\ge1/7`$. The specified starting residue classes are part of the assertion; no claim is made for every block of four consecutive indices.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.regular_rate_extraction
declarations.docstring:
**Integer extraction at a regular rate** (`long243:res:extraction`).
If `l > 1` and the positive integers `C n` satisfy
`C (n+1) / C n = 1 + l/n + o(n^{-l})`, then `l` is an integer `d ≥ 2` and
`C n = A n(n+1)⋯(n+d-1) + B` for all large `n`, with `A` a positive rational
and `B` a rational.
declarations.statement:
theorem regular_rate_extraction {l : ℝ} (hl : 1 < l) (C : ℕ → ℤ)
    (hpos : ∀ n, 0 < C n)
    (hratio : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ l * rateError l (fun j => (C j : ℝ)) n)
      atTop (nhds 0)) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, 2 ≤ d ∧ l = (d : ℝ) ∧
      ∃ A B : ℚ, 0 < A ∧ ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n, N ≤ n →
        (C n : ℝ) = (A : ℝ) * risingPow d (n : ℝ) + (B : ℝ)

results.label: long243:res:tailratio
results.title: comparison of the numerator and denominator ratios
results.statement_markdown:
*Let $`a_n`$ be strictly increasing positive integers with $`a_{n+1}/a_n^2\to1`$ and $`\sum_n1/a_n`$ rational, and let $`(C_n,D_n)`$ be the integer tail. Write $`\gamma_n=a_n^2/a_{n+1}-1`$. Then
``` math
\frac{C_{n+1}}{C_n}=1+\gamma_n+O(a_n^{-1}),
 \qquad a_n\ge\exp(c\,2^n)\ \text{eventually for some }c>0 .
```*

lean.relation_note: The Lean statement bounds the error explicitly, $|C_{n+1}/C_n-a_n^2/a_{n+1}|\le16/a_n$ for all large $n$; since $a_n^2/a_{n+1}=1+\gamma_n$, this gives the printed $O(a_n^{-1})$, and the growth bound $a_n\ge\exp(c\,2^n)$ is as printed. Lean indexes the sequence from $0$; the first conclusion is unchanged by this shift, and the second holds after replacing $c$ by $c/2$.

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR7.canonical_tail_ratio_quantitative
declarations.statement:
theorem canonical_tail_ratio_quantitative
    (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : StrictMono a) (hpos : ∀ n, 0 < a n)
    (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q)
    (hs : HasSum (fun n ↦ 1 / (a n : ℝ)) ((p : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)))
    (hgrowth : Tendsto (fun n ↦ (a (n + 1) : ℝ) / (a n : ℝ) ^ 2)
      atTop (nhds 1)) :
    let C := canonicalNaturalNumerator a p q
    (∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n →
      |(C (n + 1) : ℝ) / (C n : ℝ) -
        (a n : ℝ) ^ 2 / (a (n + 1) : ℝ)| ≤ 16 / (a n : ℝ)) ∧
    (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n →
      Real.exp (c * (2 : ℝ) ^ n) ≤ (a n : ℝ))

results.label: long243:res:update
results.title: update law
results.statement_markdown:
*For all $`a,D,C\in\mathbb{Z}`$,
``` math
aC-D=C-\bigl(D-(a-1)C\bigr).
```
Consequently, every solution of (19) satisfies $`C_{n+1}=C_n-E_n`$.*

theorem nextTailState_eq_sub_centered (a D C : ℤ) :
    nextTailState a D C = C - centeredState a D C

results.label: long243:res:scale
results.title: scaling the numerator and denominator
results.statement_markdown:
*For every $`s,a,D,C\in\mathbb{Z}`$,
``` math
a(sD)=s\,(aD),\qquad
 a(sC)-sD=s\,(aC-D),
```
``` math
sD-(a-1)sC=s\,[D-(a-1)C].
```*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR7.state_scale
declarations.docstring:
Long record `res:scale`: a single declaration covering all three
homogeneity assertions, not just one of their existing component lemmas.
declarations.statement:
theorem state_scale (s a D C : ℤ) :
    nextDenState a (s * D) = s * nextDenState a D ∧
    nextTailState a (s * D) (s * C) = s * nextTailState a D C ∧
    centeredState a (s * D) (s * C) = s * centeredState a D C

    nextDenState a (s * D) = s * nextDenState a D ∧
    nextTailState a (s * D) (s * C) = s * nextTailState a D C ∧
    centeredState a (s * D) (s * C) = s * centeredState a D C

results.label: long243:res:defect
results.title: defect identity
results.statement_markdown:
*For all $`a,a',D,C\in\mathbb{Z}`$,
``` math
\begin{aligned}
 \relax[a'-(a^2-a+1)]\,(aC-D)
 &=a^2[D-(a-1)C]\\
 &\quad-\bigl[aD-(a'-1)(aC-D)\bigr],
 \end{aligned}
```
that is, $`\Delta_n\,C_{n+1}=a_n^{2}E_n-E_{n+1}`$.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.sylvesterDefect_mul_nextTailState
declarations.docstring:
Exact defect equation from the packet:
`Δₙ Cₙ₊₁ = aₙ² Eₙ - Eₙ₊₁`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sylvesterDefect_mul_nextTailState
    (a aNext D C : ℤ) :
    sylvesterDefect a aNext * nextTailState a D C =
      a ^ 2 * centeredState a D C -
        centeredState aNext (nextDenState a D) (nextTailState a D C)

challenge.statement:
theorem sylvesterDefect_mul_nextTailState
    (a aNext D C : ℤ) :
    sylvesterDefect a aNext * nextTailState a D C =
      a ^ 2 * centeredState a D C -
        centeredState aNext (nextDenState a D) (nextTailState a D C)

results.label: long243:res:step
results.title: two vanishing errors force the step
results.statement_markdown:
*Let $`a,a',D,C\in\mathbb{Z}`$ with $`aC-D\ne0`$. If
``` math
D-(a-1)C=0,\qquad aD-(a'-1)(aC-D)=0,
```
then $`a'=a^2-a+1`$.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.sylvesterNext_eq_of_centered_zero
declarations.docstring:
If two consecutive centered errors vanish and the next tail state is
nonzero, the defect identity forces the original denominator sequence to take
the exact Sylvester step.
declarations.statement:
theorem sylvesterNext_eq_of_centered_zero
    (a aNext D C : ℤ)
    (hCnext : nextTailState a D C ≠ 0)
    (hE : centeredState a D C = 0)
    (hEnext :
      centeredState aNext (nextDenState a D) (nextTailState a D C) = 0) :
    aNext = sylvesterNext a

challenge.statement:
theorem sylvesterNext_eq_of_centered_zero
    (a aNext D C : ℤ)
    (hCnext : nextTailState a D C ≠ 0)
    (hE : centeredState a D C = 0)
    (hEnext :
      centeredState aNext (nextDenState a D) (nextTailState a D C) = 0) :
    aNext = sylvesterNext a

results.label: long243:res:secondorder
results.title: eliminating the denominator from two steps
results.statement_markdown:
*Let $`a,a_1,u,u_1,u_2,v,v_1,h,h_1`$ be integers satisfying
``` math
hu_1+v=au,\qquad hv_1=av,\qquad h_1u_2+v_1=a_1u_1.
```
Then $`a^2u+hh_1u_2=h(a+a_1)u_1`$.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR7.reduced_second_order_int
declarations.docstring:
Long record `res:secondorder`: the paper quantifies over integers.
The supplied `reducedStep_secondOrder` only quantifies over naturals.
declarations.statement:
theorem reduced_second_order_int
    (a aNext u uNext uNextNext v vNext h hNext : ℤ)
    (hu : h * uNext + v = a * u)
    (hv : h * vNext = a * v)
    (huNext : hNext * uNextNext + vNext = aNext * uNext) :
    a ^ 2 * u + h * hNext * uNextNext =
      h * (a + aNext) * uNext

challenge.statement:
theorem reduced_second_order_int
    (a aNext u uNext uNextNext v vNext h hNext : ℤ)
    (hu : h * uNext + v = a * u)
    (hv : h * vNext = a * v)
    (huNext : hNext * uNextNext + vNext = aNext * uNext) :
    a ^ 2 * u + h * hNext * uNextNext =
      h * (a + aNext) * uNext

results.label: long243:res:curvature
results.title: a square identity without cancellation
results.statement_markdown:
*Let $`a,a_1,p,p_1,p_2,q`$ be integers with $`q=ap-p_1`$ and $`p_2+a^2p=(a+a_1)p_1`$. Then
``` math
q^2+\bigl(pp_2-p_1^2\bigr)=(a_1-a)pp_1.
```*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.cancellationFree_curvature_square
declarations.docstring:
Exact square/curvature identity on a cancellation-free pair of steps.
It packages the primitive second-order cocycle as a changing quadratic norm,
without asserting the still-open global anti-shadowing conclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem cancellationFree_curvature_square
    {a aNext p pNext pNextNext q : ℤ}
    (hq : q = a * p - pNext)
    (hrec : pNextNext + a ^ 2 * p = (a + aNext) * pNext) :
    q ^ 2 + (p * pNextNext - pNext ^ 2) =
      (aNext - a) * p * pNext

challenge.statement:
theorem cancellationFree_curvature_square
    {a aNext p pNext pNextNext q : ℤ}
    (hq : q = a * p - pNext)
    (hrec : pNextNext + a ^ 2 * p = (a + aNext) * pNext) :
    q ^ 2 + (p * pNextNext - pNext ^ 2) =
      (aNext - a) * p * pNext

results.label: long243:res:oldmodulussaturation
results.title: saturation modulo an old denominator
results.statement_markdown: *Let $`M\ge2`$. Any finite word $`r_0,\ldots,r_k`$ of units modulo $`M`$ is compatible with the cancellation-free recurrences modulo $`M`$, with all reduced denominator residues equal to zero. Consequently the eliminated two-step identity alone imposes no further restriction on such unit words when the multiplier residues are free.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.unit_word_saturates_old_modulus
declarations.docstring:
**Saturation modulo an old denominator (`long243:res:oldmodulussaturation`).**
Let `M ≥ 2` and let `r 0, …, r k` be any word of units modulo `M`.  Then there
are multiplier residues `a` and denominator residues `v` modulo `M`, with every
`v i` equal to zero, satisfying the cancellation-free recurrences on the word;
the eliminated two-step identity then holds automatically, so it alone imposes
no restriction on the unit word.
declarations.statement:
theorem unit_word_saturates_old_modulus
    (M : ℕ) (hM : 2 ≤ M) (k : ℕ) (r : ℕ → ZMod M)
    (hr : ∀ i, i ≤ k → IsUnit (r i)) :
    ∃ a v : ℕ → ZMod M,
      (∀ i, i ≤ k → v i = 0) ∧
      (∀ i, i < k → r (i + 1) + v i = a i * r i) ∧
      (∀ i, i < k → v (i + 1) = a i * v i) ∧
      (∀ i, i + 2 ≤ k →
        r (i + 2) = (a i + a (i + 1)) * r (i + 1) - a i ^ 2 * r i)

challenge.statement:
theorem unit_word_saturates_old_modulus
    (M : ℕ) (hM : 2 ≤ M) (k : ℕ) (r : ℕ → ZMod M)
    (hr : ∀ i, i ≤ k → IsUnit (r i)) :
    ∃ a v : ℕ → ZMod M,
      (∀ i, i ≤ k → v i = 0) ∧
      (∀ i, i < k → r (i + 1) + v i = a i * r i) ∧
      (∀ i, i < k → v (i + 1) = a i * v i) ∧
      (∀ i, i + 2 ≤ k →
        r (i + 2) = (a i + a (i + 1)) * r (i + 1) - a i ^ 2 * r i)

results.label: long243:res:eventual
results.title: sequence form
results.statement_markdown: *Let $`a,D,C:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}`$ satisfy $`D_{n+1}=a_nD_n`$ and $`C_{n+1}=a_nC_n-D_n`$. If $`E_n=0`$ for all sufficiently large $`n`$ and $`C_{n+1}\ne0`$ for all sufficiently large $`n`$, then $`a_{n+1}=a_n^{2}-a_n+1`$ for all sufficiently large $`n`$.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.sylvesterNext_eventually_of_centered_zero
declarations.docstring:
Along an exact product-cleared tail orbit, eventual vanishing of the
centered state and eventual nonvanishing of the next tail force the exact
Sylvester recurrence from some index onward.
declarations.statement:
theorem sylvesterNext_eventually_of_centered_zero
    (a D C : ℕ → ℤ)
    (hD : ∀ n, D (n + 1) = nextDenState (a n) (D n))
    (hC : ∀ n, C (n + 1) = nextTailState (a n) (D n) (C n))
    (hE : ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → centeredState (a n) (D n) (C n) = 0)
    (hCne : ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → C (n + 1) ≠ 0) :
    ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → a (n + 1) = sylvesterNext (a n)

challenge.statement:
theorem sylvesterNext_eventually_of_centered_zero
    (a D C : ℕ → ℤ)
    (hD : ∀ n, D (n + 1) = nextDenState (a n) (D n))
    (hC : ∀ n, C (n + 1) = nextTailState (a n) (D n) (C n))
    (hE : ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → centeredState (a n) (D n) (C n) = 0)
    (hCne : ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → C (n + 1) ≠ 0) :
    ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → a (n + 1) = sylvesterNext (a n)

results.label: long243:res:absorb
results.title: zero is absorbing
results.statement_markdown: *Let $`a,C,D:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}`$ satisfy $`C_{n+1}+D_n=a_nC_n`$ and $`D_{n+1}=a_nD_n`$, and put $`E_n=D_n-(a_n-1)C_n`$. Suppose that $`|E_n|<C_n`$ for every $`n`$. If $`E_n=0`$ then $`E_{n+1}=0`$.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.centeredState_zero_absorbing
declarations.docstring:
A zero centered state is absorbing under the strict centered-representative
bound at the next index.  The defect identity makes `Cₙ₊₁` divide `Eₙ₊₁`, and
the only multiple with smaller absolute value is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem centeredState_zero_absorbing
    (a C D : ℕ → ℕ) (E : ℕ → ℤ)
    (hC : ∀ n, C (n + 1) + D n = a n * C n)
    (hD : ∀ n, D (n + 1) = a n * D n)
    (hE : ∀ n, E n = centeredState (a n : ℤ) (D n : ℤ) (C n : ℤ))
    (hcentered : ∀ n, Int.natAbs (E n) < C n)
    (n : ℕ) (hzero : E n = 0) :
    E (n + 1) = 0

challenge.statement:
theorem centeredState_zero_absorbing
    (a C D : ℕ → ℕ) (E : ℕ → ℤ)
    (hC : ∀ n, C (n + 1) + D n = a n * C n)
    (hD : ∀ n, D (n + 1) = a n * D n)
    (hE : ∀ n, E n = centeredState (a n : ℤ) (D n : ℤ) (C n : ℤ))
    (hcentered : ∀ n, Int.natAbs (E n) < C n)
    (n : ℕ) (hzero : E n = 0) :
    E (n + 1) = 0

results.label: long243:res:arithmeticrecord
results.title: boundedness and a weighted sum over new maxima
results.statement_markdown:
*Let $`a_n,L_n,U_n`$ be positive integers and $`V_n`$ integers satisfying
``` math
\begin{gathered}
 L_{n+1}=\operatorname{lcm}(L_n,a_n),\qquad \rho_n=\gcd(L_n,a_n),\\
 \rho_nU_{n+1}=U_n-V_n,\qquad
 V_n=L_n-(a_n-1)U_n,\qquad -U_n\le2V_n.
 \end{gathered}
```
Let $`f:[1,\infty)\to[0,\infty)`$ be finite and nonincreasing, with $`\int_1^\infty f(t)\,dt=\infty`$. For each fixed integer $`B\ge0`$,
``` math
\sup_n U_n<\infty
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \sum_{n\in\mathcal R}(-V_n-B)_+f(U_n)<\infty.
```*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR11.arithmetic_weighted_record_dichotomy
declarations.docstring:
**Arithmetic weighted-record dichotomy (exact printed endpoint).**

Positive integer sequences `a,L,U` and integer errors `V` satisfy the exact
LCM update, centred state update, error identity and lower centring bound.
For every fixed baseline `B` and every finite nonnegative nonincreasing weight
whose improper integral from one is unbounded, bounded height is equivalent
to finiteness of the weighted raw record-excess series.
declarations.statement:
theorem arithmetic_weighted_record_dichotomy
    (a L U : ℕ → ℕ) (V : ℕ → ℤ)
    (ha : ∀ n, 0 < a n) (hLpos : ∀ n, 0 < L n) (hU : ∀ n, 0 < U n)
    (hL : ∀ n, L (n + 1) = Nat.lcm (L n) (a n))
    (hstate : ∀ n, (Nat.gcd (L n) (a n) : ℤ) * U (n + 1) =
      (U n : ℤ) - V n)
    (herror : ∀ n, V n = (L n : ℤ) - ((a n : ℤ) - 1) * U n)
    (hcenter : ∀ n, -(U n : ℤ) ≤ 2 * V n)
    (B : ℕ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : AntitoneOn f (Set.Ici 1))
    (hpos : ∀ x : ℝ, 1 ≤ x → 0 ≤ f x) (hdiv : IntegralUnbounded f) :
    (∃ H : ℕ, ∀ n, U n ≤ H) ↔ Summable (paperRecordCharge U V B f)

challenge.statement:
theorem arithmetic_weighted_record_dichotomy
    (a L U : ℕ → ℕ) (V : ℕ → ℤ)
    (ha : ∀ n, 0 < a n) (hLpos : ∀ n, 0 < L n) (hU : ∀ n, 0 < U n)
    (hL : ∀ n, L (n + 1) = Nat.lcm (L n) (a n))
    (hstate : ∀ n, (Nat.gcd (L n) (a n) : ℤ) * U (n + 1) =
      (U n : ℤ) - V n)
    (herror : ∀ n, V n = (L n : ℤ) - ((a n : ℤ) - 1) * U n)
    (hcenter : ∀ n, -(U n : ℤ) ≤ 2 * V n)
    (B : ℕ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : AntitoneOn f (Set.Ici 1))
    (hpos : ∀ x : ℝ, 1 ≤ x → 0 ≤ f x) (hdiv : IntegralUnbounded f) :
    (∃ H : ℕ, ∀ n, U n ≤ H) ↔ Summable (paperRecordCharge U V B f)

results.label: long243:res:weightedrecord
results.title: a convergent weighted sum over new maxima
results.statement_markdown:
*Assume the growth and rationality hypotheses of Problem 1.1, and let $`f`$ be as in Theorem 6.1. The sequence is eventually Sylvester if and only if, for some integer $`B\ge0`$,
``` math
\sum_{n\in\mathcal R}(-V_n-B)_+f(U_n)<\infty.
```*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR11.canonical_weighted_record_excess
declarations.docstring:
Exact short-paper weighted-record equivalence, stated with the canonical
LCM numerator constructed above and the printed raw error weight. The
baseline is existential; all previous state theorems work for every fixed B.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonical_weighted_record_excess
    (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : StrictMono a) (hapos : ∀ n, 0 < a n)
    (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q)
    (hs : HasSum (fun n ↦ 1 / (a n : ℝ)) ((p : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)))
    (hgrowth : Tendsto (fun n ↦ (a (n + 1) : ℝ) / (a n : ℝ) ^ 2)
      atTop (𝓝 1))
    (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : AntitoneOn f (Set.Ici 1))
    (hpos : ∀ x : ℝ, 1 ≤ x → 0 ≤ f x) (hdiv : IntegralUnbounded f) :
    (∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → (a (n + 1) : ℤ) = (a n : ℤ) ^ 2 - (a n : ℤ) + 1) ↔
      ∃ B : ℕ, Summable (paperRecordCharge (canonicalLcmNumerator a p q)
        (canonicalLcmDigit a p q) B f)

challenge.statement:
theorem canonical_weighted_record_excess
    (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : StrictMono a) (hapos : ∀ n, 0 < a n)
    (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q)
    (hs : HasSum (fun n ↦ 1 / (a n : ℝ)) ((p : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)))
    (hgrowth : Tendsto (fun n ↦ (a (n + 1) : ℝ) / (a n : ℝ) ^ 2)
      atTop (𝓝 1))
    (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : AntitoneOn f (Set.Ici 1))
    (hpos : ∀ x : ℝ, 1 ≤ x → 0 ≤ f x) (hdiv : IntegralUnbounded f) :
    (∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → (a (n + 1) : ℤ) = (a n : ℤ) ^ 2 - (a n : ℤ) + 1) ↔
      ∃ B : ℕ, Summable (paperRecordCharge (canonicalLcmNumerator a p q)
        (canonicalLcmDigit a p q) B f)

results.label: long243:res:valuationtransition
results.title: the denominator valuation transition
results.statement_markdown:
*Let $`u,v,a`$ be positive integers, $`\gcd(u,v)=1`$, and $`w=au-v>0`$. Put $`h=\gcd(w,av)`$ and $`v'=av/h`$. For a prime $`p`$, write $`r=\nu_p(a)`$, $`s=\nu_p(v)`$ and $`t=\nu_p(w)`$. Then
``` math
\nu_p(v')=
 \begin{cases}
 \max(r,s),&r\ne s,\\
 \max(0,2s-t),&r=s.
 \end{cases}
```
In particular $`\nu_p(v')\le\max(r,s)`$. A strict loss relative to $`s`$ requires $`r=s\ge1`$ and $`t>s`$.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.reduced_denominator_valuation_transition
declarations.docstring:
**The denominator valuation transition (`long243:res:valuationtransition`).**
With `r = ν_p a`, `s = ν_p v` and `t = ν_p w`, the reduced denominator
`v' = a * v / gcd (w, a * v)` has `ν_p v' = max (r, s)` when `r ≠ s` and
`ν_p v' = max (0, 2 * s - t)` when `r = s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem reduced_denominator_valuation_transition
    {u v a w h v' p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime)
    (hu : 0 < u) (hv : 0 < v) (ha : 0 < a)
    (hcop : Nat.Coprime u v)
    (hw : w + v = a * u) (hwpos : 0 < w)
    (hh : h = Nat.gcd w (a * v))
    (hv'def : v' = a * v / h) :
    (a.factorization p ≠ v.factorization p →
        v'.factorization p = max (a.factorization p) (v.factorization p))
    ∧ (a.factorization p = v.factorization p →
        v'.factorization p
          = max 0 (2 * v.factorization p - w.factorization p))

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.reduced_denominator_valuation_le_max
declarations.docstring:
**In particular (`long243:res:valuationtransition`).**  The reduced
denominator valuation never exceeds `max (ν_p a, ν_p v)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem reduced_denominator_valuation_le_max
    {u v a w h v' p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime)
    (hu : 0 < u) (hv : 0 < v) (ha : 0 < a)
    (hcop : Nat.Coprime u v)
    (hw : w + v = a * u) (hwpos : 0 < w)
    (hh : h = Nat.gcd w (a * v))
    (hv'def : v' = a * v / h) :
    v'.factorization p ≤ max (a.factorization p) (v.factorization p)

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.reduced_denominator_valuation_strict_loss
declarations.docstring:
**In particular (`long243:res:valuationtransition`).**  A strict loss of
denominator valuation relative to `s = ν_p v` requires `ν_p a = ν_p v ≥ 1` and
`ν_p w > ν_p v`.
declarations.statement:
theorem reduced_denominator_valuation_strict_loss
    {u v a w h v' p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime)
    (hu : 0 < u) (hv : 0 < v) (ha : 0 < a)
    (hcop : Nat.Coprime u v)
    (hw : w + v = a * u) (hwpos : 0 < w)
    (hh : h = Nat.gcd w (a * v))
    (hv'def : v' = a * v / h)
    (hloss : v'.factorization p < v.factorization p) :
    a.factorization p = v.factorization p ∧ 1 ≤ v.factorization p ∧
      v.factorization p < w.factorization p

challenge.statement:
theorem reduced_denominator_valuation_transition
    {u v a w h v' p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime)
    (hu : 0 < u) (hv : 0 < v) (ha : 0 < a)
    (hcop : Nat.Coprime u v)
    (hw : w + v = a * u) (hwpos : 0 < w)
    (hh : h = Nat.gcd w (a * v))
    (hv'def : v' = a * v / h) :
    (a.factorization p ≠ v.factorization p →
        v'.factorization p = max (a.factorization p) (v.factorization p))
    ∧ (a.factorization p = v.factorization p →
        v'.factorization p
          = max 0 (2 * v.factorization p - w.factorization p))

theorem reduced_denominator_valuation_le_max
    {u v a w h v' p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime)
    (hu : 0 < u) (hv : 0 < v) (ha : 0 < a)
    (hcop : Nat.Coprime u v)
    (hw : w + v = a * u) (hwpos : 0 < w)
    (hh : h = Nat.gcd w (a * v))
    (hv'def : v' = a * v / h) :
    v'.factorization p ≤ max (a.factorization p) (v.factorization p)

theorem reduced_denominator_valuation_strict_loss
    {u v a w h v' p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime)
    (hu : 0 < u) (hv : 0 < v) (ha : 0 < a)
    (hcop : Nat.Coprime u v)
    (hw : w + v = a * u) (hwpos : 0 < w)
    (hh : h = Nat.gcd w (a * v))
    (hv'def : v' = a * v / h)
    (hloss : v'.factorization p < v.factorization p) :
    a.factorization p = v.factorization p ∧ 1 ≤ v.factorization p ∧
      v.factorization p < w.factorization p

results.label: long243:res:powerpersistence
results.title: persistence of a prime power
results.statement_markdown: *Suppose $`p^k\mid v_s`$. If $`w_n<p^{k+1}`$ at every step from $`s`$ through $`t-1`$, then $`p^k\mid v_t`$.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR20.primePower_persists
declarations.docstring:
**Persistence of a prime power (`long243:res:powerpersistence`).**
If `p ^ k` divides the reduced denominator at time `s`, and every raw next
numerator on `[s,t)` is below `p ^ (k+1)`, then `p ^ k` still divides the
reduced denominator at time `t`.

This is an interval induction using `primitive_valuation_no_drop`; its
hypotheses spell out exactly the standing primitive reduced-tail recurrence
used by the paper.
declarations.statement:
theorem primePower_persists
    (a u v w hc : ℕ → ℕ) {p k s t : ℕ}
    (hp : p.Prime)
    (hst : s ≤ t)
    (hcop : ∀ n, Nat.Coprime (u n) (v n))
    (hvpos : ∀ n, 0 < v n)
    (hq : ∀ n, w n + v n = a n * u n)
    (hwpos : ∀ n, 0 < w n)
    (hnum : ∀ n, w n = hc n * u (n + 1))
    (hden : ∀ n, a n * v n = hc n * v (n + 1))
    (hstart : p ^ k ∣ v s)
    (hsmall : ∀ n, s ≤ n → n < t → w n < p ^ (k + 1)) :
    p ^ k ∣ v t

challenge.statement:
theorem primePower_persists
    (a u v w hc : ℕ → ℕ) {p k s t : ℕ}
    (hp : p.Prime)
    (hst : s ≤ t)
    (hcop : ∀ n, Nat.Coprime (u n) (v n))
    (hvpos : ∀ n, 0 < v n)
    (hq : ∀ n, w n + v n = a n * u n)
    (hwpos : ∀ n, 0 < w n)
    (hnum : ∀ n, w n = hc n * u (n + 1))
    (hden : ∀ n, a n * v n = hc n * v (n + 1))
    (hstart : p ^ k ∣ v s)
    (hsmall : ∀ n, s ≤ n → n < t → w n < p ^ (k + 1)) :
    p ^ k ∣ v t

results.label: long243:res:recorddichotomy
results.title: increments of the running maximum
results.statement_markdown: *Let $`\Theta=\limsup_n(H_{n+1}-H_n)/\ell(H_n)`$ on a rational-tail orbit under the standing hypotheses, and suppose $`E_n`$ is not eventually zero. Then either $`G_n`$ is unbounded and $`\Theta`$ is infinite, or $`G_n`$ stabilises at a value $`g`$ and $`\Theta\ge g\,v_T/\varphi(v_T)`$ for every late $`T`$, so that $`\Theta>g\ge1`$. For any orbit under the standing hypotheses, therefore, $`\Theta=0`$ or $`\Theta>1`$, and $`\Theta\le1`$ forces the eventual Sylvester recurrence.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR11.canonical_quantitative_record_dichotomy
declarations.docstring: The complete quantitative statement on the actual canonical orbit.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonical_quantitative_record_dichotomy
    (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : StrictMono a) (hapos : ∀ n, 0 < a n)
    (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q)
    (hs : HasSum (fun n ↦ 1 / (a n : ℝ)) ((p : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)))
    (hgrowth : Tendsto (fun n ↦ (a (n + 1) : ℝ) / (a n : ℝ) ^ 2) atTop (𝓝 1))
    (hnot : ¬ ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → (a (n + 1) : ℤ) = sylvesterNext (a n : ℤ)) :
    let C := canonicalNaturalNumerator a p q
    let D := canonicalDenominator a q
    ((∀ B : ℕ, ∃ n, B < Nat.gcd (C n) (D n)) ∧ recordTheta C = ⊤) ∨
    ∃ N g : ℕ, 0 < g ∧ (∀ n, N ≤ n → Nat.gcd (C n) (D n) = g) ∧
      (∀ T : ℕ, N + 2 ≤ T →
        (((g : ℝ) * (D T / g : ℕ) / Nat.totient (D T / g) : ℝ) : EReal) ≤ recordTheta C) ∧
      (g : EReal) < recordTheta C

declarations.statement:
theorem canonical_recordTheta_zero_or_gt_one
    (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : StrictMono a) (hapos : ∀ n, 0 < a n)

    (hs : HasSum (fun n ↦ 1 / (a n : ℝ)) ((p : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)))

    recordTheta (canonicalNaturalNumerator a p q) = 0 ∨
      (1 : EReal) < recordTheta (canonicalNaturalNumerator a p q)

results.label: long243:res:loglogboundary
results.title: the double-logarithmic bound
results.statement_markdown:
*If
``` math
\limsup_n\frac{(-E_n)_+}{\ell(C_n)}\le1,
```
then the sequence is eventually Sylvester. Every counterexample therefore satisfies
``` math
\limsup_n\frac{(-E_n)_+}{\ell(C_n)}>1.
```*

hypotheses are retained; no conditional CRT or prime supplier is assumed.

results.label: long243:res:recordamplified
results.title: bounds allowing for previous decreases
results.statement_markdown: *Under the standing hypotheses, the following are equivalent: eventual Sylvester behaviour; $`\limsup_n\mathcal A_n<\infty`$; $`\limsup_nR_n\delta_n<\infty`$. Each of those two limits superior is $`0`$ or $`+\infty`$.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.StandingOrbit.recordAmplified
declarations.docstring:
**`long243:res:recordamplified` (bounds allowing for previous decreases).**

Under the standing hypotheses the following are equivalent: eventual Sylvester
behaviour; `limsup 𝒜 n < ∞`; `limsup (R n δ n) < ∞`.  Each of those two limits
superior is `0` or `+∞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem recordAmplified :
    (O.EventuallySylvester ↔
        Filter.limsup (fun n ↦ ((O.amp n : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop ≠ ⊤) ∧
      (O.EventuallySylvester ↔
        Filter.limsup (fun n ↦ (((O.R n : ℝ) * O.delta n : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop ≠ ⊤) ∧
      (Filter.limsup (fun n ↦ ((O.amp n : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop = 0 ∨
        Filter.limsup (fun n ↦ ((O.amp n : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop = ⊤) ∧
      (Filter.limsup (fun n ↦ (((O.R n : ℝ) * O.delta n : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop = 0 ∨
        Filter.limsup (fun n ↦ (((O.R n : ℝ) * O.delta n : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop = ⊤)

declarations.statement:
theorem amp_bddAbove_iff_sylvester :
    O.EventuallySylvester ↔ ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, O.amp n ≤ K

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.StandingOrbit.Rdelta_bddAbove_iff_amp
declarations.statement:

      (∃ K : ℝ, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (O.R n : ℝ) * O.delta n ≤ K)

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.StandingOrbit.eventuallySylvester_of_amp_le
declarations.docstring:
**`𝒜 n ≤ K` eventually forces an eventually Sylvester tail.**

This is the `K`-increment cut for an arbitrarily cancelled reduced orbit: the
bound gives `m n ≤ K`, hence `u (n+1) ≤ u n + K`, and `h s < 2K`; `K` distinct
primes above `2K` are then locked into the reduced denominator at a common late
index `T`, a CRT block of `K` consecutive integers above `R T` is placed on
them, and the forced first crossing must land inside the block.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventuallySylvester_of_amp_le (K : ℕ) (hK1 : 1 ≤ K) (N₀ : ℕ)
    (hbd : ∀ n, N₀ ≤ n → O.amp n ≤ (K : ℝ)) : O.EventuallySylvester

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.StandingOrbit.coprimeMultiplier_cofinal
declarations.docstring:
**Cofinal supply of coprime multipliers.**  A multiplier coprime to the
accumulated denominator occurs at arbitrarily late indices.  This is the
qualitative content of the density-one count in the proof of
`long243:res:recorddichotomy`; only the finite telescoping identity is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem coprimeMultiplier_cofinal (N : ℕ) :
    ∃ n, N ≤ n ∧ Nat.Coprime (O.a n) (O.D n)

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.StandingOrbit.largePrime_coprimeMultiplier
declarations.docstring:
**Coprime multipliers with a large prime factor occur cofinally.**

Distinct coprime-multiplier steps use disjoint sets of primes, because a prime
that has already entered the accumulated denominator cannot divide a later
coprime multiplier.  Only finitely many primes lie below `B`, so beyond every
index there is a coprime multiplier step whose multiplier has a prime factor
exceeding `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem largePrime_coprimeMultiplier (B : ℕ) (N : ℕ) :
    ∃ n, N ≤ n ∧ Nat.Coprime (O.a n) (O.D n) ∧
      ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ p ∣ O.a n ∧ B < p

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.StandingOrbit.primeBlock_supply
declarations.docstring:
**The protected prime block.**  If every cancellation factor beyond `N₀` is
at most `B`, then for every `j` there is an index `T ≥ N₀` and a set of `j`
distinct primes above `B`, all dividing `v T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem primeBlock_supply (B N₀ : ℕ) (hcanc : ∀ m, N₀ ≤ m → O.canc m ≤ B) :
    ∀ j : ℕ, ∃ T, N₀ ≤ T ∧ ∃ P : Finset ℕ, P.card = j ∧
      ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p ∧ B < p ∧ p ∣ O.v T

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.StandingOrbit.canc_lt_of_amp_le
declarations.docstring:
**The estimate at the first later negative error.**  With `𝒜 n ≤ K`
eventually, `𝒜 t ≥ u s / u (s+1)` at the first later negative-error index `t`,
so `2 h s ≤ 3 K` and hence `h s < 2 K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canc_lt_of_amp_le (hns : ¬ O.EventuallySylvester) (K : ℕ) (hK1 : 1 ≤ K)
    (N₀ : ℕ) (hbd : ∀ n, N₀ ≤ n → O.amp n ≤ (K : ℝ)) :
    ∃ N, ∀ s, N ≤ s → O.canc s < 2 * K

results.label: long243:res:criticalrate
results.title: the critical rate
results.statement_markdown: *Under the standing hypotheses and $`\delta_n=O(1/n)`$, with no convergence of $`n\delta_n`$ assumed, eventual Sylvester behaviour is equivalent to $`u_n=O(n)`$ and to $`(-\tilde e_n)_+=O(1)`$. A counterexample at the critical rate therefore has $`\limsup_nu_n/n=\infty`$ and $`\limsup_n(-\tilde e_n)_+=\infty`$.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.StandingOrbit.criticalRate
declarations.docstring:
**`long243:res:criticalrate` (the critical rate).**

Under the standing hypotheses and `δ n = O(1/n)`, with no convergence of
`n δ n` assumed, eventual Sylvester behaviour is equivalent to `u n = O(n)` and
to `(-ẽ n)₊ = O(1)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem criticalRate
    (hδ : (fun n : ℕ ↦ O.delta n) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ 1 / (n : ℝ))) :
    (O.EventuallySylvester ↔ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (O.u n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ))) ∧
      (O.EventuallySylvester ↔
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ (O.negPart n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun _ : ℕ ↦ (1 : ℝ)))

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.StandingOrbit.criticalRate_counterexample
declarations.docstring:
A counterexample at the critical rate has `limsup u n / n = ∞` and
`limsup (-ẽ n)₊ = ∞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem criticalRate_counterexample
    (hδ : (fun n : ℕ ↦ O.delta n) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ 1 / (n : ℝ)))
    (hns : ¬ O.EventuallySylvester) :
    Filter.limsup (fun n ↦ (((O.u n : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop = ⊤ ∧
      Filter.limsup (fun n ↦ ((O.negPart n : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop = ⊤

theorem criticalRate_counterexample (O : StandingOrbit)
    (hδ : (fun n : ℕ ↦ O.delta n) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ 1 / (n : ℝ)))
    (hns : ¬ O.EventuallySylvester) :
    Filter.limsup (fun n ↦ (((O.u n : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop = ⊤ ∧
      Filter.limsup (fun n ↦ ((O.negPart n : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop = ⊤

theorem R_le_of_u_le (O : StandingOrbit) {c N : ℕ} (h : ∀ n, N ≤ n → O.u n ≤ c * n) :
    ∀ n, N ≤ n → O.R n ≤ O.R N + c * n

results.label: long243:res:oddpowersupply
results.title: large odd prime powers in the reduced denominator
results.statement_markdown:
*Under the standing hypotheses, for every fixed $`A>0`$ and every sufficiently large $`n`$, the reduced denominator $`v_n`$ has an odd prime-power divisor $`Q=p^k`$ with
``` math
Q>(H_n+2)^A,\qquad H_n=\max_{j\le n}C_j.
```
The prime $`p`$ may depend on $`n`$; no stable-gcd or prime-arrival assumption is imposed.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.StandingOrbit.oddPrimePower_supply
declarations.docstring:
**`long243:res:oddpowersupply`: large odd prime powers in the reduced
denominator.**

Under the standing hypotheses, for every fixed real `A > 0` and every
sufficiently large `n`, the reduced denominator `v n` has an odd prime-power
divisor `Q = p ^ k` with `Q > (H n + 2) ^ A`, where `H n = max_{j ≤ n} C j`.
The prime `p` may depend on `n`; no stable-gcd or prime-arrival assumption is
imposed.
declarations.statement:
theorem oddPrimePower_supply (A : ℝ) (hA : 0 < A) :
    ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → ∃ p k : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ p ≠ 2 ∧ 1 ≤ k ∧ Odd (p ^ k) ∧
      p ^ k ∣ O.v n ∧ ((O.Hmax n : ℝ) + 2) ^ A < ((p ^ k : ℕ) : ℝ)

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.StandingOrbit.oddPrimePower_supply_nat
declarations.docstring:
**Large odd prime powers in the reduced denominator, natural exponent.**

For every natural `A` and every sufficiently large `n`, the reduced
denominator `v n` has an odd prime-power divisor `p ^ k > (Hmax n + 2) ^ A`.
The prime `p` may depend on `n`; no stable-gcd or prime-arrival assumption
is imposed.
declarations.statement:
theorem oddPrimePower_supply_nat (A : ℕ) :
    ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → ∃ p k : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ p ≠ 2 ∧ 1 ≤ k ∧
      p ^ k ∣ O.v n ∧ (O.Hmax n + 2) ^ A < p ^ k

challenge.statement:
theorem oddPrimePower_supply (O : StandingOrbit) (A : ℝ) (hA : 0 < A) :
    ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → ∃ p k : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ p ≠ 2 ∧ 1 ≤ k ∧ Odd (p ^ k) ∧
      p ^ k ∣ O.v n ∧ ((O.Hmax n : ℝ) + 2) ^ A < ((p ^ k : ℕ) : ℝ)

theorem oddPrimePower_supply_nat (O : StandingOrbit) (A : ℕ) :
    ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → ∃ p k : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ p ≠ 2 ∧ 1 ≤ k ∧
      p ^ k ∣ O.v n ∧ (O.Hmax n + 2) ^ A < p ^ k

results.label: long243:res:unitrecord
results.title: unit record increments
results.statement_markdown: *Under the standing hypotheses, if $`R_{n+1}-R_n\le1`$ for all large $`n`$, then $`a_{n+1}=a_n^2-a_n+1`$ for all large $`n`$. Hence the sequence is eventually Sylvester if and only if $`\#\{n:R_{n+1}-R_n\ge2\}`$ is finite. No hypothesis is placed on decreases in $`u_n`$, on record-setting jumps, or on the cancellation factors $`h_n`$.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.StandingOrbit.unitRecordIncrement_sylvesterNext
declarations.docstring:
**`long243:res:unitrecord` (i): unit record increments force the Sylvester
recurrence.**

Under the standing hypotheses, if `R (n+1) - R n ≤ 1` for all large `n`, then
`a (n+1) = a n ^ 2 - a n + 1` for all large `n`.  No hypothesis is placed on
drawdowns, on record-setting jumps, or on the cancellation factors `h n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem unitRecordIncrement_sylvesterNext
    (hinc : ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → O.R (n + 1) - O.R n ≤ 1) :
    ∃ M, ∀ n, M ≤ n → (O.a (n + 1) : ℤ) = (O.a n : ℤ) ^ 2 - (O.a n : ℤ) + 1

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.StandingOrbit.unitRecordIncrement_criterion
declarations.docstring:
**`long243:res:unitrecord` (ii): the finiteness criterion.**

The sequence is eventually Sylvester if and only if
`#{n : R (n+1) - R n ≥ 2}` is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem unitRecordIncrement_criterion :
    (∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → (O.a (n + 1) : ℤ) = (O.a n : ℤ) ^ 2 - (O.a n : ℤ) + 1) ↔
      {n : ℕ | 2 ≤ O.R (n + 1) - O.R n}.Finite

challenge.statement:
theorem unitRecordIncrement_sylvesterNext (O : StandingOrbit)
    (hinc : ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → O.R (n + 1) - O.R n ≤ 1) :
    ∃ M, ∀ n, M ≤ n → (O.a (n + 1) : ℤ) = (O.a n : ℤ) ^ 2 - (O.a n : ℤ) + 1

theorem unitRecordIncrement_criterion (O : StandingOrbit) :
    (∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → (O.a (n + 1) : ℤ) = (O.a n : ℤ) ^ 2 - (O.a n : ℤ) + 1) ↔
      {n : ℕ | 2 ≤ O.R (n + 1) - O.R n}.Finite

results.label: long243:res:epochenergy
results.title: counting crossings before a prime power is lost
results.statement_markdown: *Let the orbit satisfy the reduced recurrences of this section, with $`2|\tilde e_n|<u_n`$ from an index $`s`$. Let $`p\ge3`$ be prime, $`Q=p^{\ell}`$ divide $`v_s`$ with $`Q\ge16`$, put $`L=pQ/2`$, and assume $`R_s<L/2`$. Assume that $`u_t\ge L`$ for some $`t>s`$, and let $`\tau`$ be the first such index, let $`J`$ be the set of steps in $`[s,\tau)`$ that first cross at least one odd multiple of $`p`$ in $`(L/2,L]`$, and put $`X=\sum_{n\in J}(d_n-2)`$. Then every $`n\in J`$ is a record step with $`h_n=1`$ and $`d_n\ge3`$, and $`pQ\le(8p+8)\lvert J\rvert+4X+8p`$.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.epoch_energy_named_crossing_set
declarations.docstring:
**Counting crossings before a prime power is lost
(`long243:res:epochenergy`).**

Let the orbit satisfy the reduced recurrences of the section with
`2 * |ẽ n| < u n` from an index `s`, where `ẽ n = u n - w n`.  Let `p ≥ 3` be
prime, let `Q = p ^ l` divide `v s` with `Q ≥ 16`, put `L = p * Q / 2` and
assume `R s < L / 2`.  Assume `u t ≥ L` for some `t > s` and let `τ` be the
first such index.  Let `J` be the set of steps in `[s, τ)` that first cross at
least one odd multiple of `p` in `(L/2, L]`, and put
`X = ∑_{n ∈ J} (d n - 2)`.  Then every `n ∈ J` is a record step with
`h n = 1` and `d n ≥ 3`, and `p * Q ≤ (8p+8) * |J| + 4 * X + 8p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem epoch_energy_named_crossing_set
    (a u v w hc : ℕ → ℕ) (p l s τ : ℕ) (J : Finset ℕ)
    (hp : p.Prime)
    (hp3 : 3 ≤ p)
    (hred : ∀ n, s ≤ n → Nat.Coprime (u n) (v n))
    (hvpos : ∀ n, s ≤ n → 0 < v n)
    (hw : ∀ n, s ≤ n → w n + v n = a n * u n)
    (hwpos : ∀ n, s ≤ n → 0 < w n)
    (hnum : ∀ n, s ≤ n → w n = hc n * u (n + 1))
    (hden : ∀ n, s ≤ n → a n * v n = hc n * v (n + 1))
    (hcentre : ∀ n, s ≤ n → 2 * ((u n : ℤ) - (w n : ℤ)).natAbs < u n)
    (hprot : p ^ l ∣ v s)
    (hQ : 16 ≤ p ^ l)
    (hRs : 4 * runningMax u s < p * p ^ l)
    (hsτ : s < τ)
    (hτ : p * p ^ l ≤ 2 * u τ)
    (hτfirst : ∀ n, s < n → n < τ → 2 * u n < p * p ^ l)
    (hJ : ∀ n, n ∈ J ↔ (s ≤ n ∧ n < τ ∧ ∃ b : ℕ, Odd b ∧ p ∣ b ∧
      p * p ^ l < 4 * b ∧ 2 * b ≤ p * p ^ l ∧
      b ≤ u (n + 1) ∧ ∀ j, s ≤ j → j < n → u (j + 1) < b)) :
    (∀ n ∈ J, runningMax u n < u (n + 1) ∧ hc n = 1 ∧ u n + 3 ≤ u (n + 1)) ∧
      p * p ^ l ≤ (8 * p + 8) * J.card
        + 4 * ∑ n ∈ J, (u (n + 1) - u n - 2) + 8 * p

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.mem_barrierIdx_iff
declarations.docstring:
`barrierIdx Q` is exactly the index set of the odd multiples `(2 * k + 1)`
of the window condition: the barrier `(2 * k + 1) * p` lies in
`(p * Q / 4, p * Q / 2]` precisely for `k ∈ barrierIdx Q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_barrierIdx_iff {Q : ℕ} (hQ : 16 ≤ Q) (k : ℕ) :
    k ∈ barrierIdx Q ↔ Q < 4 * (2 * k + 1) ∧ 2 * (2 * k + 1) ≤ Q

challenge.statement:
theorem epoch_energy_named_crossing_set
    (a u v w hc : ℕ → ℕ) (p l s τ : ℕ) (J : Finset ℕ)
    (hp : p.Prime)
    (hp3 : 3 ≤ p)
    (hred : ∀ n, s ≤ n → Nat.Coprime (u n) (v n))
    (hvpos : ∀ n, s ≤ n → 0 < v n)
    (hw : ∀ n, s ≤ n → w n + v n = a n * u n)
    (hwpos : ∀ n, s ≤ n → 0 < w n)
    (hnum : ∀ n, s ≤ n → w n = hc n * u (n + 1))
    (hden : ∀ n, s ≤ n → a n * v n = hc n * v (n + 1))
    (hcentre : ∀ n, s ≤ n → 2 * ((u n : ℤ) - (w n : ℤ)).natAbs < u n)
    (hprot : p ^ l ∣ v s)
    (hQ : 16 ≤ p ^ l)
    (hRs : 4 * runningMax u s < p * p ^ l)
    (hsτ : s < τ)
    (hτ : p * p ^ l ≤ 2 * u τ)
    (hτfirst : ∀ n, s < n → n < τ → 2 * u n < p * p ^ l)
    (hJ : ∀ n, n ∈ J ↔ (s ≤ n ∧ n < τ ∧ ∃ b : ℕ, Odd b ∧ p ∣ b ∧
      p * p ^ l < 4 * b ∧ 2 * b ≤ p * p ^ l ∧
      b ≤ u (n + 1) ∧ ∀ j, s ≤ j → j < n → u (j + 1) < b)) :
    (∀ n ∈ J, runningMax u n < u (n + 1) ∧ hc n = 1 ∧ u n + 3 ≤ u (n + 1)) ∧
      p * p ^ l ≤ (8 * p + 8) * J.card
        + 4 * ∑ n ∈ J, (u (n + 1) - u n - 2) + 8 * p

theorem mem_barrierIdx_iff {Q : ℕ} (hQ : 16 ≤ Q) (k : ℕ) :
    k ∈ barrierIdx Q ↔ Q < 4 * (2 * k + 1) ∧ 2 * (2 * k + 1) ≤ Q

results.label: long243:res:energycriterion
results.title: two convergence criteria for large record jumps
results.statement_markdown:
*Under the standing hypotheses, the sum $`\mathcal E=\sum_{n\ \mathrm{record}}\bigl(\mathbf 1_{d_n\ge3}u_n^{-1/2}
+(d_n-2)_+u_n^{-1}\bigr)`$ is finite if and only if the sequence is eventually Sylvester; and $`\sum_{n\ \mathrm{record}}(d_n-2)_+u_n^{-1/2}`$ is finite if and only if the sequence is eventually Sylvester.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.StandingOrbit.energy_criterion
declarations.docstring:
**`long243:res:energycriterion` in full**: both series are finite exactly
when the sequence is eventually Sylvester, so in particular they are finite
together.
declarations.statement:
theorem energy_criterion :
    (Summable O.energy ↔
        ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → (O.a (n + 1) : ℤ) = (O.a n : ℤ) ^ 2 - (O.a n : ℤ) + 1) ∧
      (Summable O.energySqrt ↔
        ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → (O.a (n + 1) : ℤ) = (O.a n : ℤ) ^ 2 - (O.a n : ℤ) + 1)

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.StandingOrbit.energy_summable_iff
declarations.docstring:
**`long243:res:energycriterion`, first series.**

`𝓔 = ∑_{n record} (1_{d_n ≥ 3} u_n^{-1/2} + (d_n - 2)_+ u_n^{-1})` is finite if
and only if the sequence is eventually Sylvester.
declarations.statement:
theorem energy_summable_iff :
    Summable O.energy ↔
      ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → (O.a (n + 1) : ℤ) = (O.a n : ℤ) ^ 2 - (O.a n : ℤ) + 1

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.StandingOrbit.energySqrt_summable_iff
declarations.docstring:
**`long243:res:energycriterion`, second series.**

`∑_{n record} (d_n - 2)_+ u_n^{-1/2}` is finite if and only if the sequence is
eventually Sylvester.
declarations.statement:
theorem energySqrt_summable_iff :
    Summable O.energySqrt ↔
      ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → (O.a (n + 1) : ℤ) = (O.a n : ℤ) ^ 2 - (O.a n : ℤ) + 1

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.StandingOrbit.energy_le_two_energySqrt
declarations.docstring:
**The paper's term-by-term comparison.**  At a record,
`1_{d ≥ 3} u^{-1/2} + (d-2)_+ u^{-1} ≤ 2 (d-2)_+ u^{-1/2}`.
declarations.statement: theorem energy_le_two_energySqrt (n : ℕ) : O.energy n ≤ 2 * O.energySqrt n

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.StandingOrbit.exists_late_energy_window
declarations.docstring:
**The paper's window estimate.**  If the reduced numerator is unbounded then
for every `S` there are `S ≤ s < τ` and a finite set `J ⊆ [s, τ)` of record
steps with `d_n ≥ 3` whose energy contribution is at least `1/16`.

The prime power comes from `long243:res:oddpowersupply` at `A = 3`, the set `J`
and the counting inequality from `long243:res:epochenergy`, and the passage to
the real series from `energy_window_real_bound`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_late_energy_window (hunb : ∀ M : ℕ, ∃ n, M < O.u n) (S : ℕ) :
    ∃ (s τ : ℕ) (J : Finset ℕ), S ≤ s ∧ s < τ ∧ (∀ n ∈ J, s ≤ n ∧ n < τ) ∧
      (1 : ℝ) / 16 ≤ ∑ n ∈ J, O.energy n

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.energy_window_real_bound
declarations.docstring:
**The real-valued division of the counting inequality.**

This is the displayed step in the proof of `long243:res:energycriterion`.  With
`P = p Q`, `L = P / 2`, `Q = p ^ k ≥ 16` and `Q ≥ p ≥ 3`, the paper's two
constant estimates are `8p / L = 16 / Q ≤ 1` (here `hP16`) and
`(8p + 8) / √L ≤ 8 √2 (1 + 1/p) < 16` (here `hPsq`, since `L ≥ p² / 2`).
Dividing `P ≤ (8p+8) K + 4 X + 8p` by `L` therefore gives
`1 ≤ 16 K / √L + 4 X / L`, i.e. `1/16 ≤ K / √L + X / L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem energy_window_real_bound {pr P K X : ℝ}
    (hpr : 3 ≤ pr) (hPsq : pr * pr ≤ P) (hP16 : 16 * pr ≤ P)
    (hK : 0 ≤ K) (hX : 0 ≤ X)
    (hineq : P ≤ (8 * pr + 8) * K + 4 * X + 8 * pr) :
    (1 : ℝ) / 16 ≤ K / Real.sqrt (P / 2) + X / (P / 2)

challenge.statement:
theorem energy_criterion (O : StandingOrbit) :
    (Summable O.energy ↔
        ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → (O.a (n + 1) : ℤ) = (O.a n : ℤ) ^ 2 - (O.a n : ℤ) + 1) ∧
      (Summable O.energySqrt ↔
        ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → (O.a (n + 1) : ℤ) = (O.a n : ℤ) ^ 2 - (O.a n : ℤ) + 1)

theorem energy_summable_iff (O : StandingOrbit) :
    Summable O.energy ↔
      ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → (O.a (n + 1) : ℤ) = (O.a n : ℤ) ^ 2 - (O.a n : ℤ) + 1

theorem energySqrt_summable_iff (O : StandingOrbit) :
    Summable O.energySqrt ↔
      ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → (O.a (n + 1) : ℤ) = (O.a n : ℤ) ^ 2 - (O.a n : ℤ) + 1
theorem energy_le_two_energySqrt (O : StandingOrbit) (n : ℕ) : O.energy n ≤ 2 * O.energySqrt n

theorem exists_late_energy_window (O : StandingOrbit) (hunb : ∀ M : ℕ, ∃ n, M < O.u n) (S : ℕ) :
    ∃ (s τ : ℕ) (J : Finset ℕ), S ≤ s ∧ s < τ ∧ (∀ n ∈ J, s ≤ n ∧ n < τ) ∧
      (1 : ℝ) / 16 ≤ ∑ n ∈ J, O.energy n

theorem energy_window_real_bound {pr P K X : ℝ}
    (hpr : 3 ≤ pr) (hPsq : pr * pr ≤ P) (hP16 : 16 * pr ≤ P)
    (hK : 0 ≤ K) (hX : 0 ≤ X)
    (hineq : P ≤ (8 * pr + 8) * K + 4 * X + 8 * pr) :
    (1 : ℝ) / 16 ≤ K / Real.sqrt (P / 2) + X / (P / 2)

results.label: long243:res:slownegative
results.title: slow negative part
results.statement_markdown: *Let $`a,C,D:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}`$ satisfy (19) with $`a_n>1`$, $`C_n>0`$, $`D_0\ge1`$, under vanishing relative error. Suppose that for some $`\delta\in(0,1)`$ and all large $`n`$ with $`E_n<0`$ one has $`-E_n\le(1-\delta)\ell(C_n)`$. Then $`E_n=0`$ for all large $`n`$, and $`a_{n+1}=a_n^2-a_n+1`$ for all large $`n`$.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.slowNegative_eventually_zero_and_sylvesterNext_unconditional
declarations.docstring:
**`long243:res:slownegative` (core.tex:2203), with no extra hypothesis.**

Let `(a, C, D)` be an exact orbit of natural numbers with `a_n > 1`, `C_n > 0`,
`D_0 ≥ 1`, under vanishing relative error.  Suppose that for some
`δ ∈ (0,1)` and all large `n` with `E_n < 0` one has
`-E_n ≤ (1-δ) ℓ(C_n)`.  Then `E_n = 0` for all large `n`, and
`a_{n+1} = a_n² - a_n + 1` for all large `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem slowNegative_eventually_zero_and_sylvesterNext_unconditional
    (a C D : ℕ → ℕ) (E : ℕ → ℤ) (δ : ℝ)
    (ha : ∀ n, 1 < a n)
    (hCpos : ∀ n, 0 < C n)
    (hD0 : 1 ≤ D 0)
    (hC : ∀ n, C (n + 1) + D n = a n * C n)
    (hDstep : ∀ n, D (n + 1) = a n * D n)
    (hE : ∀ n, E n = centeredState (a n : ℤ) (D n : ℤ) (C n : ℤ))
    (hvanish : ∀ K, ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → K * Int.natAbs (E n) < C n)
    (hδ0 : 0 < δ) (hδ1 : δ < 1)
    (hslow : ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → E n < 0 →
      -((E n : ℤ) : ℝ) ≤ (1 - δ) * recordLogLog ((C n : ℕ) : ℝ)) :
    (∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → E n = 0) ∧
      ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → (a (n + 1) : ℤ) = sylvesterNext (a n : ℤ)

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.exactOrbit_recordTheta_gt_one
declarations.docstring:
**The paper's auxiliary lower bound `Θ ≥ 1` for a general exact orbit.**

Let `(a, C, D)` be an exact orbit of natural numbers with `a_n > 1`, `C_n > 0`,
`D_0 ≥ 1`, under vanishing relative error, and suppose the centred error is not
eventually zero.  Then `1 < Θ`, where
`Θ = limsup (H_{n+1} - H_n) / ℓ(H_n)` and `H_n = max_{j ≤ n} C_j`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exactOrbit_recordTheta_gt_one
    (a C D : ℕ → ℕ) (E : ℕ → ℤ)
    (ha : ∀ n, 1 < a n) (hCpos : ∀ n, 0 < C n) (hD0 : 1 ≤ D 0)
    (hC : ∀ n, C (n + 1) + D n = a n * C n)
    (hD : ∀ n, D (n + 1) = a n * D n)
    (hE : ∀ n, E n = centeredState (a n : ℤ) (D n : ℤ) (C n : ℤ))
    (hvanish : ∀ K, ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → K * Int.natAbs (E n) < C n)
    (hnot : ¬ ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → E n = 0) :
    (1 : EReal) < recordTheta C

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.exactOrbit_one_le_recordTheta
declarations.docstring:
The paper's auxiliary lower bound in the form the slow-negative argument
consumes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exactOrbit_one_le_recordTheta
    (a C D : ℕ → ℕ) (E : ℕ → ℤ)
    (ha : ∀ n, 1 < a n) (hCpos : ∀ n, 0 < C n) (hD0 : 1 ≤ D 0)
    (hC : ∀ n, C (n + 1) + D n = a n * C n)
    (hD : ∀ n, D (n + 1) = a n * D n)
    (hE : ∀ n, E n = centeredState (a n : ℤ) (D n : ℤ) (C n : ℤ))
    (hvanish : ∀ K, ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → K * Int.natAbs (E n) < C n)
    (hnot : ¬ ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → E n = 0) :
    (1 : EReal) ≤ recordTheta C

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.exactOrbit_unbounded_of_error_not_eventually_zero
declarations.docstring:
If the centred error is not eventually zero then `C n → ∞`.  Zero is
absorbing on the tail where `|E n| < C n`, so the error is nowhere zero there
and `tailState_tendsto_atTop_of_nonzero_normalizedVanishes` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem exactOrbit_unbounded_of_error_not_eventually_zero
    (a C D : ℕ → ℕ) (E : ℕ → ℤ)
    (hC : ∀ n, C (n + 1) + D n = a n * C n)
    (hD : ∀ n, D (n + 1) = a n * D n)

results.label: long243:res:strausbounded
results.title: bounded or slowly growing increments of the product ratio
results.statement_markdown:
*Let $`a_1<a_2<\cdots`$ be positive integers with $`a_{n+1}/a_n^2\to1`$ and $`\sum_{n\ge1}1/a_n=p/q`$, where $`p,q`$ are positive integers. Put
``` math
Q_n=\frac{a_1a_2\cdots a_{n-1}}{a_n}
     \left(\frac{a_n^2}{a_{n+1}}-1\right).
```
If $`\limsup_nQ_n<\infty`$, the sequence is eventually Sylvester. The same conclusion holds if, for some $`\delta>0`$ and all large $`n`$,
``` math
Q_n\le\frac{1-\delta}{q}\,
 \ell(a_1\cdots a_{n-1}/a_n).
```*

by p/q and the finite upper limsup represented by eventual boundedness.
This is an end-to-end source candidate: the integer state, analytic
hypotheses and bounded negative error are all derived, not assumed.

declarations.docstring:
**The slow-growth clause of `long243:res:strausbounded`.**
Let `a₁ < a₂ < ⋯` be positive integers with `a_{n+1}/a_n² → 1` and
`∑ 1/a_n = p/q` with `q` a positive integer.  If for some `δ > 0` and all
large `n`

`Q_n ≤ ((1-δ)/q) ℓ(a_1 ⋯ a_{n-1} / a_n)`,  `ℓ(x) = log₂ log₂ max(4,x)`,

then `a_{n+1} = a_n² - a_n + 1` for all large `n`.

    (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : StrictMono a) (hpos : ∀ n, 0 < a n)
    (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q)

    (hgrowth : Tendsto (fun n ↦ (a (n + 1) : ℝ) / (a n : ℝ) ^ 2)
      atTop (nhds 1))
    (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ)
    (hslow : ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n →
      productDefect a n ≤ (1 - δ) / (q : ℝ) *
        recordLogLog ((prefixProduct a n : ℝ) / (a n : ℝ))) :

      (a (n + 1) : ℤ) = (a n : ℤ) ^ 2 - (a n : ℤ) + 1

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.recordTheta_le_of_slow_negative
declarations.docstring:
**The record-coefficient form of the slow negative part.**
For any exact orbit `C_{n+1} + D_n = a_n C_n` with centred error
`E_n = D_n - (a_n - 1) C_n`, an eventual bound `-E_n ≤ c ℓ(C_n)` with `c ≥ 0`
forces `Θ = recordTheta C ≤ c`.

The step is the paper's: `C_{n+1} = C_n - E_n`, and `C_n` never exceeds its own
running maximum, so a new record can overshoot the old one by at most `-E_n`;
`ℓ` is monotone, so `ℓ(C_n) ≤ ℓ(H_n)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem recordTheta_le_of_slow_negative
    (a C D : ℕ → ℕ) (E : ℕ → ℤ)
    (hstep : ∀ n, C (n + 1) + D n = a n * C n)
    (hE : ∀ n, E n = (D n : ℤ) - ((a n : ℤ) - 1) * (C n : ℤ))
    (c : ℝ) (hc0 : 0 ≤ c) (N : ℕ)
    (hslow : ∀ n, N ≤ n → -((E n : ℤ) : ℝ) ≤ c * recordLogLog ((C n : ℕ) : ℝ)) :
    recordTheta C ≤ ((c : ℝ) : EReal)

written argument.

    (prefixProduct a n : ℝ) / (a n : ℝ) ≤
      ((canonicalNaturalNumerator a p q n : ℕ) : ℝ)

results.label: long243:res:onethreshold
results.title: the $`1/n`$ threshold
results.statement_markdown:
*Let $`a_1<a_2<\cdots`$ be positive integers with $`a_{n+1}/a_n^2\to1`$ and $`\sum_n1/a_n\in\mathbb{Q}`$. If
``` math
\limsup_{n\to\infty} n\,(a_n^2/a_{n+1}-1)_+<1,
```
then $`a_{n+1}=a_n^2-a_n+1`$ for all large $`n`$. The same conclusion holds if, for some $`K\ge0`$ and $`\varepsilon>0`$,
``` math
\frac{a_n^2}{a_{n+1}}-1\le\frac1n+\frac{K}{n^{1+\varepsilon}}
 \quad\hbox{eventually}.
```
In particular the one-sided bound by $`1/n`$ is included.*

lean.relation_note: The strict limsup case, the bound $1/n+K/n^{1+\varepsilon}$ and the one-sided bound $1/n$ are, in that order, `original_coordinate_strict_one`, `original_coordinate_inclusive_one` and `original_coordinate_inclusive_one_pointwise`, with the limsup hypothesis written as an eventual bound by some $r<1$. Lean indexes the sequence from $0$, so in the paper's indexing its hypotheses read $(n-1)(a_n^2/a_{n+1}-1)_+\le r$ and $a_n^2/a_{n+1}-1\le1/(n-1)+K/(n-1)^{1+\varepsilon}$ eventually, and the printed hypotheses imply them.

`r < 1` with `n (a_n²/a_{n+1} - 1)_+ ≤ r` for all large `n`, then
`a_{n+1} = a_n² - a_n + 1` for all large `n`.
declarations.statement:

    (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : StrictMono a) (hpos : ∀ n, 0 < a n)

      (a n : ℝ) ^ 2 / (a (n + 1) : ℝ) - 1 ≤ 1 / (n : ℝ)) :
    ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n →
      (a (n + 1) : ℤ) = (a n : ℤ) ^ 2 - (a n : ℤ) + 1

results.label: long243:res:classicalhalfspace
results.title: comparison of the two signs
results.statement_markdown:
*The factor $`M_n=D_n/L_n`$ divides $`G_n=\gcd(C_n,D_n)`$. Thus $`G_n/M_n`$ is a positive integer and $`E_n/M_n=(G_n/M_n)\tilde e_n`$ is an integer with the same sign as $`E_n`$. The sign of the growth ratio minus one also depends on a correction term. The exact recurrences give, whenever $`a_{n+1}C_nC_{n+1}\ne0`$,
``` math
\begin{equation}
\label{long243:eq:shiftedsign}
 \frac{a_n^2}{a_{n+1}}-1=-\frac{E_n}{C_n}+\Lambda_n,
 \qquad
 \Lambda_n=\frac{\bigl(1-E_n/C_n\bigr)\bigl(a_n-1+E_{n+1}/C_{n+1}\bigr)}{a_{n+1}},
\end{equation}
```
and, under the standing positive rational-tail hypotheses, $`0<\Lambda_n<3/a_n`$ for all sufficiently large $`n`$. The Erdős–Straus quantity of Theorem 3 is
``` math
Z_n^{\mathrm{ES}}=
 \frac{[a_1,\ldots,a_n]}{a_{n+1}}
 \left(\frac{a_{n+1}^2}{a_{n+2}}-1\right).
```
Its least common multiple includes $`a_n`$ but not the clearing denominator $`q`$. It is not $`Q_n=(P_n/a_n)\gamma_n`$ from the preceding subsection, nor $`L_n\gamma_{n+1}/a_{n+1}`$ under our convention $`L_n=\operatorname{lcm}(q,a_1,\ldots,a_{n-1})`$. Being a positive multiple of the next growth defect, $`Z_n^{\mathrm{ES}}`$ has the sign of $`\Lambda_{n+1}-E_{n+1}/C_{n+1}`$. For all sufficiently large $`n`$, it is positive when $`E_{n+1}\le0`$; for $`E_{n+1}>0`$, it is negative precisely when $`E_{n+1}/C_{n+1}>\Lambda_{n+1}`$. Under the eventual Sylvester recurrence, $`E_n=0`$ and $`\Lambda_n=(a_n-1)/a_{n+1}>0`$.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.overlapDebt_dvd_gcd
declarations.docstring:
**First clause of `long243:res:classicalhalfspace`.**
The clearing factor `M_n = D_n/L_n` is a positive integer dividing
`G_n = gcd(C_n, D_n)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem overlapDebt_dvd_gcd
    (a : ℕ → ℕ) (hpos : ∀ n, 0 < a n) (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (n : ℕ) :
    0 < cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n ∧
      cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n *  cumulativeDigitLcm q a n =
        canonicalDenominator a q n ∧
      cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n ∣
        Nat.gcd (canonicalNaturalNumerator a p q n) (canonicalDenominator a q n)

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.canonicalError_div_overlapDebt
declarations.docstring:
**Second clause of `long243:res:classicalhalfspace`.**
`G_n/M_n` is a positive integer, `E_n/M_n = (G_n/M_n) ẽ_n` with
`ẽ_n = E_n/G_n`, and `E_n/M_n` has the same sign as `E_n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalError_div_overlapDebt
    (a : ℕ → ℕ) (hpos : ∀ n, 0 < a n) (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (n : ℕ) :
    0 < Nat.gcd (canonicalNaturalNumerator a p q n) (canonicalDenominator a q n) /
        cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n ∧
      ((cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n : ℕ) : ℤ) ∣ canonicalError a p q n ∧
      ((Nat.gcd (canonicalNaturalNumerator a p q n)
          (canonicalDenominator a q n) : ℕ) : ℤ) ∣ canonicalError a p q n ∧
      canonicalError a p q n / ((cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n : ℕ) : ℤ) =
        ((Nat.gcd (canonicalNaturalNumerator a p q n) (canonicalDenominator a q n) /
            cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n : ℕ) : ℤ) *
          (canonicalError a p q n /
            ((Nat.gcd (canonicalNaturalNumerator a p q n)
              (canonicalDenominator a q n) : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
      (0 < canonicalError a p q n ↔
        0 < canonicalError a p q n / ((cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
      (canonicalError a p q n < 0 ↔
        canonicalError a p q n / ((cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n : ℕ) : ℤ) < 0) ∧
      (canonicalError a p q n = 0 ↔
        canonicalError a p q n / ((cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n : ℕ) : ℤ) = 0)

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.growthDefect_eq_neg_relativeError_add_shiftedCorrection
declarations.docstring:
**The identity `long243:eq:shiftedsign`.**
For the exact recurrences `D_{n+1} = a_n D_n`, `C_{n+1} = a_n C_n - D_n` and
the centred error `E_n = D_n - (a_n - 1) C_n`, whenever `a_{n+1} C_n C_{n+1} ≠ 0`,

`a_n²/a_{n+1} - 1 = -E_n/C_n + Λ_n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem growthDefect_eq_neg_relativeError_add_shiftedCorrection
    {a aNext D DNext C CNext E ENext : ℝ}
    (hD : DNext = a * D)
    (hC : CNext = a * C - D)
    (hE : E = D - (a - 1) * C)
    (hENext : ENext = DNext - (aNext - 1) * CNext)
    (hne : aNext * C * CNext ≠ 0) :
    a ^ 2 / aNext - 1 =
      -(E / C) + shiftedCorrectionTerm a aNext C CNext E ENext

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.canonical_growthDefect_identity
declarations.docstring: **The identity `long243:eq:shiftedsign` on the canonical orbit.**
declarations.statement:
theorem canonical_growthDefect_identity
    (a : ℕ → ℕ) (hpos : ∀ n, 0 < a n) (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q)
    (hs : HasSum (fun n ↦ 1 / (a n : ℝ)) ((p : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))) (n : ℕ) :
    (a n : ℝ) ^ 2 / (a (n + 1) : ℝ) - 1 =
      -(((canonicalError a p q n : ℤ) : ℝ) /
          ((canonicalNaturalNumerator a p q n : ℕ) : ℝ)) +
        canonicalCorrection a p q n

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.canonicalCorrection_pos_and_lt_three_div
declarations.docstring: **The eventual bound `0 < Λ_n < 3/a_n` under the standing hypotheses.**
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalCorrection_pos_and_lt_three_div
    (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : StrictMono a) (hpos : ∀ n, 0 < a n)
    (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q)
    (hs : HasSum (fun n ↦ 1 / (a n : ℝ)) ((p : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)))
    (hgrowth : Tendsto (fun n ↦ (a (n + 1) : ℝ) / (a n : ℝ) ^ 2)
      atTop (nhds 1)) :
    ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n →
      0 < canonicalCorrection a p q n ∧
        canonicalCorrection a p q n < 3 / (a n : ℝ)

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.shiftedCorrectionTerm_pos_and_lt_three_div
declarations.docstring:
The eventual bound `0 < Λ_n < 3/a_n`, in the abstract form in which it is
used: `a_n ≥ 2`, `a_{n+1} ≥ a_n²/2`, and both relative errors at most `1/4`.
declarations.statement:
theorem shiftedCorrectionTerm_pos_and_lt_three_div
    {A ANext C CNext E ENext : ℝ}
    (hA : 2 ≤ A) (hANext : A ^ 2 / 2 ≤ ANext)
    (hθ : |E / C| ≤ 1 / 4) (hθNext : |ENext / CNext| ≤ 1 / 4) :
    0 < shiftedCorrectionTerm A ANext C CNext E ENext ∧
      shiftedCorrectionTerm A ANext C CNext E ENext < 3 / A

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.erdosStraus_lcm_includes_digit_not_denominator
declarations.docstring:
The least common multiple in `Z_n^ES` includes `a_n`, and is the `q = 1`
cumulative one, so it does not include the clearing denominator.
declarations.statement:
theorem erdosStraus_lcm_includes_digit_not_denominator (a : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) :
    cumulativeDigitLcm 1 a (n + 1) = Nat.lcm (cumulativeDigitLcm 1 a n) (a n) ∧
      a n ∣ cumulativeDigitLcm 1 a (n + 1) ∧
      cumulativeDigitLcm 1 a 0 = 1

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.erdosStrausQuantity_ne_productDefect_ne_lcmShift
declarations.docstring:
`Z_n^ES` is not the product quantity `Q_n = (P_n/a_n) γ_n`, and it is not
`L_n γ_{n+1}/a_{n+1}` for the convention `L_n = lcm(q, a_0, …, a_{n-1})`.
The witness is `a_j = j + 2`, `q = 7`, `n = 1`, where the three values are
`33/10`, `5/6` and `77/10`.
declarations.statement:
theorem erdosStrausQuantity_ne_productDefect_ne_lcmShift :
    ∃ (a : ℕ → ℕ) (q n : ℕ), 0 < q ∧ (∀ m, 0 < a m) ∧
      erdosStrausQuantity a n ≠ productDefect a n ∧
      erdosStrausQuantity a n ≠
        (cumulativeDigitLcm q a n : ℝ) *
          ((a (n + 1) : ℝ) ^ 2 / (a (n + 2) : ℝ) - 1) / (a (n + 1) : ℝ)

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.erdosStrausQuantity_sign
declarations.docstring:
**The sign clauses of `long243:res:classicalhalfspace`.**
`Z_n^ES` is a positive multiple of the next growth defect, so it has the sign of
`Λ_{n+1} - E_{n+1}/C_{n+1}`; for all sufficiently large `n` it is positive when
`E_{n+1} ≤ 0`, and for `E_{n+1} > 0` it is negative exactly when
`E_{n+1}/C_{n+1} > Λ_{n+1}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem erdosStrausQuantity_sign
    (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : StrictMono a) (hpos : ∀ n, 0 < a n)
    (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q)
    (hs : HasSum (fun n ↦ 1 / (a n : ℝ)) ((p : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)))
    (hgrowth : Tendsto (fun n ↦ (a (n + 1) : ℝ) / (a n : ℝ) ^ 2)
      atTop (nhds 1)) :
    ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n →
      (0 < erdosStrausQuantity a n ↔
        ((canonicalError a p q (n + 1) : ℤ) : ℝ) /
            ((canonicalNaturalNumerator a p q (n + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) <
          canonicalCorrection a p q (n + 1)) ∧
      (erdosStrausQuantity a n < 0 ↔
        canonicalCorrection a p q (n + 1) <
          ((canonicalError a p q (n + 1) : ℤ) : ℝ) /
            ((canonicalNaturalNumerator a p q (n + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ)) ∧
      (canonicalError a p q (n + 1) ≤ 0 → 0 < erdosStrausQuantity a n) ∧
      (0 < canonicalError a p q (n + 1) →
        (erdosStrausQuantity a n < 0 ↔
          canonicalCorrection a p q (n + 1) <
            ((canonicalError a p q (n + 1) : ℤ) : ℝ) /
              ((canonicalNaturalNumerator a p q (n + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ)))

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.sylvesterTail_shiftedCorrection
declarations.docstring:
**The Sylvester-tail clause of `long243:res:classicalhalfspace`.**
If `E_n = 0` and `a_{n+1} = a_n² - a_n + 1`, then `E_{n+1} = 0` and
`Λ_n = (a_n - 1)/a_{n+1} > 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sylvesterTail_shiftedCorrection
    {a aNext D DNext C CNext E ENext : ℝ}
    (hD : DNext = a * D)
    (hC : CNext = a * C - D)
    (hE : E = D - (a - 1) * C)
    (hENext : ENext = DNext - (aNext - 1) * CNext)
    (ha : 1 < a)
    (hsyl : aNext = a ^ 2 - a + 1)
    (hzero : E = 0) :
    ENext = 0 ∧
      shiftedCorrectionTerm a aNext C CNext E ENext = (a - 1) / aNext ∧
      0 < shiftedCorrectionTerm a aNext C CNext E ENext

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.overlapDebt_mul_lcmClearedNumerator
declarations.docstring:
`C_n = M_n U_n`: the product-cleared numerator is the clearing factor times
the LCM-cleared numerator.
declarations.statement:
theorem overlapDebt_mul_lcmClearedNumerator
    (a : ℕ → ℕ) (hpos : ∀ n, 0 < a n) (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (n : ℕ) :
    ((cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n : ℕ) : ℤ) * lcmClearedNumerator a p q n =
      clearedIntegerNumerator a p q n

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.digitProductScale_eq_canonicalDenominator
declarations.docstring:
The cumulative product scale is the canonical product-cleared denominator
`D_n = q P_n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem digitProductScale_eq_canonicalDenominator (q : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) :
    digitProductScale q a n = canonicalDenominator a q n

theorem shiftedCorrectionTerm_pos_and_lt_three_div

theorem erdosStrausQuantity_sign

results.label: long243:res:coprimalitycap
results.title: an elementary interval bound
results.statement_markdown:
*Let $`m_0<m_1<\cdots`$ be pairwise coprime integers at least $`2`$ with $`\theta=\sum_i1/m_i<1`$. For all integers $`x\ge1`$ and $`L\ge1`$ satisfying $`L>k/(1-\theta)`$, where $`k=\#\{i:m_i\le x+L\}`$, the interval $`[x,x+L)`$ contains an integer divisible by no $`m_i`$. If also $`\ell(m_i)=i+O(1)`$, then for every $`\epsilon>0`$ there are an index $`T`$ and a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers $`(u_n)`$ such that
``` math
m_i\nmid u_n\quad\text{for every }i\ge T\text{ and every }n,
 \qquad
 u_{n+1}-u_n\le(1+\epsilon)\ell(u_n)\quad\text{eventually}.
```*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.exists_avoiding_in_window
declarations.docstring:
Clause (i) of `long243:res:coprimalitycap`: for pairwise coprime moduli
`m 0 < m 1 < ⋯`, all at least `2`, with `θ = ∑ᵢ 1/mᵢ < 1`, every window
`[x, x+L)` with `x ≥ 1`, `L ≥ 1` and `L > k/(1-θ)`, where `k = #{i : mᵢ ≤ x+L}`,
contains an integer divisible by no `mᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_avoiding_in_window
    {m : ℕ → ℕ} (hmono : StrictMono m) (hm2 : ∀ i, 2 ≤ m i)
    (hcop : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Nat.Coprime (m i) (m j))
    {θ : ℝ} (hsum : Summable fun i => (1 : ℝ) / (m i : ℝ))
    (hθ : ∑' i, (1 : ℝ) / (m i : ℝ) = θ) (hθ1 : θ < 1)
    {x L : ℕ} (hx : 1 ≤ x) (hL : 1 ≤ L)
    (hkL : ((({i | m i ≤ x + L} : Set ℕ).ncard : ℝ)) / (1 - θ) < (L : ℝ)) :
    ∃ n, x ≤ n ∧ n < x + L ∧ ∀ i, ¬ m i ∣ n

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.exists_slow_rise_avoiding_sequence
declarations.docstring:
Clause (ii) of `long243:res:coprimalitycap`.  If in addition
`ℓ(mᵢ) = i + O(1)`, then for every `ε > 0` there are an index `T` and a
strictly increasing sequence `(uₙ)` of positive integers such that `mᵢ ∤ uₙ`
for every `i ≥ T` and every `n`, and `u_{n+1} - uₙ ≤ (1+ε) ℓ(uₙ)` eventually.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_slow_rise_avoiding_sequence
    {m : ℕ → ℕ} (hmono : StrictMono m) (hm2 : ∀ i, 2 ≤ m i)
    (hcop : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Nat.Coprime (m i) (m j))

results.label: long243:res:constant
results.title: no constant negative magnitude
results.statement_markdown: *For any $`m,c\in\mathbb{N}`$ with $`m>0`$, there is no pair of sequences $`a,D:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}`$ with $`a_n\ge2`$ for all $`n`$ satisfying $`D_{n+1}=a_nD_n`$ and ({5.1}). The same holds if the identity is assumed only from some index onwards.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.no_constantNegative_shapeEquation
declarations.docstring:
**No constant negative magnitude (`long243:res:constant`), first clause.**
For any `m, c : ℕ` with `m > 0`, there is no pair of sequences
`a, D : ℕ → ℕ` with `aₙ ≥ 2` for all `n` satisfying `Dₙ₊₁ = aₙ Dₙ` and the
shape equation `Dₙ + m = (aₙ - 1)(c + n m)` of `(5.1)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem no_constantNegative_shapeEquation
    (m c : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) :
    ¬ ∃ a D : ℕ → ℕ,
      (∀ n, 2 ≤ a n) ∧
      (∀ n, D (n + 1) = a n * D n) ∧
      (∀ n, D n + m = (a n - 1) * (c + n * m))

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.no_eventuallyConstantNegative_shapeEquation
declarations.docstring:
**No constant negative magnitude (`long243:res:constant`), second clause:
"the same holds if the shape equation only begins at some index".**
Here the shape equation is read from index `N` on, with the numerator
restarted at `c = C N`, so that at index `N + n` it reads
`D (N + n) + m = (a (N + n) - 1) (c + n m)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem no_eventuallyConstantNegative_shapeEquation
    (m c N : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) :
    ¬ ∃ a D : ℕ → ℕ,
      (∀ n, 2 ≤ a n) ∧
      (∀ n, D (n + 1) = a n * D n) ∧
      (∀ n, D (N + n) + m = (a (N + n) - 1) * (c + n * m))

challenge.statement:
theorem no_constantNegative_shapeEquation

results.label: long243:res:periodic
results.title: no periodic negative magnitude
results.statement_markdown:
*Let $`a,D,C,e:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}`$ with $`a_n\ge2`$, $`e_n>0`$ and $`e_n<a_n`$ for every $`n`$, satisfying
``` math
D_{n+1}=a_nD_n,\qquad C_{n+1}=C_n+e_n,\qquad D_n+e_n=(a_n-1)C_n ,
```
and suppose $`e_{n+h}=e_n`$ and $`C_{n+h}=C_n+M`$ for some $`h>0`$ and $`M>0`$. This is impossible.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.no_periodicNegative_shapeEquation
declarations.docstring:
**No periodic negative magnitude (`long243:res:periodic`).**
There are no `a, D, C, e : ℕ → ℕ` with `aₙ ≥ 2`, `eₙ > 0` and `eₙ < aₙ` for
every `n`, satisfying `Dₙ₊₁ = aₙ Dₙ`, `Cₙ₊₁ = Cₙ + eₙ` and
`Dₙ + eₙ = (aₙ - 1) Cₙ`, with `eₙ₊ₕ = eₙ` and `Cₙ₊ₕ = Cₙ + M` for some
`h > 0` and `M > 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem no_periodicNegative_shapeEquation
    (h M : ℕ) (hh : 0 < h) (hM : 0 < M) :
    ¬ ∃ a D C e : ℕ → ℕ,
      (∀ n, 2 ≤ a n) ∧
      (∀ n, 0 < e n) ∧
      (∀ n, e n < a n) ∧
      (∀ n, D (n + 1) = a n * D n) ∧
      (∀ n, C (n + 1) = C n + e n) ∧
      (∀ n, D n + e n = (a n - 1) * C n) ∧
      (∀ n, e (n + h) = e n) ∧
      (∀ n, C (n + h) = C n + M)

challenge.statement:
theorem no_periodicNegative_shapeEquation
    (h M : ℕ) (hh : 0 < h) (hM : 0 < M) :
    ¬ ∃ a D C e : ℕ → ℕ,
      (∀ n, 2 ≤ a n) ∧
      (∀ n, 0 < e n) ∧
      (∀ n, e n < a n) ∧
      (∀ n, D (n + 1) = a n * D n) ∧
      (∀ n, C (n + 1) = C n + e n) ∧
      (∀ n, D n + e n = (a n - 1) * C n) ∧
      (∀ n, e (n + h) = e n) ∧
      (∀ n, C (n + h) = C n + M)

results.label: long243:res:crt
results.title: shifted blocks of consecutive multiples
results.statement_markdown: *Let $`m_0,\ldots,m_{B-1}`$ be pairwise coprime and at least $`2`$. For every bound there is a $`t`$ beyond it with $`m_i\mid t+i`$ for each $`i<B`$.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.exists_shiftedBlock_consecutiveMultiples
declarations.docstring:
**Shifted blocks of consecutive multiples (`long243:res:crt`).**
Let `m 0, …, m (B-1)` be pairwise coprime and at least `2`.  For every bound
`L` there is a `t` beyond it with `m i ∣ t + i` for each `i < B`.
declarations.statement:

results.label: long243:res:barrier
results.title: bounded increases and coprimality to earlier moduli
results.statement_markdown: *Let $`u:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}`$ tend to infinity with $`u_{n+1}\le u_n+B`$ for a fixed integer $`B\ge1`$. Then $`u`$ cannot remain coprime to infinitely many fresh pairwise coprime moduli: there is no family of pairwise coprime $`m_i\ge2`$, one for each index, such that $`\gcd(m_i,u_t)=1`$ whenever $`i<t`$.*

declarations.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos243.PaperCompleteR21.no_boundedRise_coprimeToEarlierModuli
declarations.docstring:
**Bounded increases and coprimality to earlier moduli
(`long243:res:barrier`).**
Let `u : ℕ → ℕ` tend to infinity with `u (n+1) ≤ u n + B` for a fixed
integer `B ≥ 1`.  Then there is no family of pairwise coprime `m i ≥ 2`, one
for each index, such that `gcd (m i) (u t) = 1` whenever `i < t`.
declarations.statement:
theorem no_boundedRise_coprimeToEarlierModuli
    (u : ℕ → ℕ) (B : ℕ) (hB : 1 ≤ B)
    (hrise : ∀ n, u (n + 1) ≤ u n + B)
    (hTop : Filter.Tendsto u Filter.atTop Filter.atTop) :
    ¬ ∃ m : ℕ → ℕ,
      (∀ i, 2 ≤ m i) ∧
      (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Nat.Coprime (m i) (m j)) ∧
      (∀ i t, i < t → Nat.gcd (m i) (u t) = 1)

challenge.statement:
theorem no_boundedRise_coprimeToEarlierModuli
    (u : ℕ → ℕ) (B : ℕ) (hB : 1 ≤ B)
